about: Player-facing fact cards for Spa City Hoops. Each restates one audited, confirmed question from games/trivia/data/questions.json (id). tools/check-facts.mjs verifies ids, confidence and sources.

facts.text: In 1912, baseball star Honus Wagner bought and donated basketball uniforms to Hot Springs High School, in the black and gold the school still wears.
Lakeside High School in Hot Springs was founded in 1928.
Lakeside High School won basketball state titles in 1945 and 2000.
Hot Springs High's girls won back-to-back state titles in 1997 and 1998. The boys also won a state title in 1998.
Arkansas high school basketball uses a 35-second shot clock, mandatory for all schools by 2022-23.
facts.source: Delta Plex News: AAA shot clock resolution

facts.text: The Arkansas Activities Association adopted the shot clock in 2020 by a vote of 183-69.
facts.source: Delta Plex News: AAA shot clock resolution

facts.text: The 2026 Arkansas high school basketball state finals were played at Bank OZK Arena in Hot Springs on March 12, 13 and 14.
facts.source: KAIT: 2026 State Basketball Finals Weekend continues in Hot Springs

facts.text: Shameka Christon, Hot Springs High class of 2000, went on to play in the WNBA.
Lakeside High lists NFL player Landon Trusty and NBA player Keljin Blevins among its notable alumni.
Lakeside High School's mascot is the Rams. Its listed rivals include the Hot Springs Trojans and Lake Hamilton Wolves.
Lakeside High School's colors are blue and gold.
Lake Hamilton High School's colors are maroon and gold. The Wolves play in Class 6A.
Lake Hamilton High School is in Pearcy, near Lake Hamilton and Lake Catherine.
The Hot Springs High School Trojans wear black and gold.
